finding.title: Fix the GoalSetupScreen "provably-dead — delete" verdict in docs/planning/on-device-preflight-cheatsheet.md before anyone acts on it

evidence.quote: Delete the whole file lib/features/scheduler/presentation/screens/goal_setup_screen.dart (both GoalSetupForm and GoalSetupScreen are dead)... Do NOT spend on-device test effort mounting GoalSetupScreen/GoalSetupForm: there is no in-app path to it.

finding.why: track_detail_screen.dart (a churn-hotspot file) wires `_openGoalEdit`, called from an onTap at line 692, which pushes `GoalSetupScreen` via `Navigator.push(MaterialPageRoute(...))` at line 788 — this is the live "Edit Goal" flow, reachable and reachable-only via Navigator (never @RoutePage-routed, which is exactly why the cheatsheet's router/`.gr.dart` grep missed it). A later doc in the same repo, e2e-test-suite-plan.md (2026-06-18), independently and correctly classifies GoalSetupScreen as reachable ("Navigator push only"), directly contradicting this cheatsheet's "provably-dead" verdict. The cheatsheet is explicitly framed as an action list ("pre-flight cheat-sheet") with an unambiguous, confident delete instruction; anyone or any agent treating it as current guidance today would delete a live, user-reachable screen — a real functional regression (the Edit-Goal button on Track Detail would 404/crash).
finding.recommendation: Strike or correct the GoalSetupScreen entry (cross-reference e2e-test-suite-plan.md's classification) and add a one-line banner to the top of the cheatsheet stating its verdicts are a snapshot as of the 2026-05-31 commit and must be re-grepped before acting, since — as this very file shows — the underlying code moves.
acceptance_criteria: The GoalSetupScreen section no longer recommends deletion, or is removed/marked resolved-incorrect.
A dated "snapshot, re-verify before acting" disclaimer is added near the top of the file.
Spot check: `grep -rn 'GoalSetupScreen(' learning_tracker/lib` continues to show the track_detail_screen.dart call site as the acceptance check that the doc no longer disagrees with.

finding.title: Update stale status/title headers in living docs/planning/ files whose own body or code shows the work is already done

evidence.quote: **Status:** Scoped, product decisions made (2026-06-14). Phase 1 in progress.
**Date:** 2026-06-18 · **Status:** Planning — implementation-ready; Wave 1 builds on proven harness...

finding.why: daf-unit-display-scope.md's own header contradicts its own footer within the same file (verified against 5 real commits: ffba2a26, 5e6ada50, f8ec2828, c6e28970, 053957a3, all present in git log). overdue-refactor-architecture.md is marked Draft, yet learning_tracker/lib/features/scheduler/.../scheduler_providers.dart:1096-1098 has a comment explicitly citing "architecture §11 step 4" as the reason the backfill machinery was deleted — the design shipped. e2e-test-suite-plan.md says "Planning"; test/e2e/journeys/ already has 35 P0/P1/P2 files and the harness it names as aspirational already exists. epics.md's title names only Epic 19 while its 854 lines run through Epic 27, all *(Done)*. None of these are factually wrong about the underlying work, but a reader skimming only the header (the common case) gets the wrong picture of what's left to do, which risks duplicate work or under-prioritizing a doc that's actually irrelevant/settled.
finding.recommendation: Refresh each header/title to match the body: daf-unit-display-scope.md and overdue-refactor-architecture.md to "Complete"/"Implemented", e2e-test-suite-plan.md's status to reflect Wave 1-3 progress against the 35 existing journey files, and epics.md's title to name the full epic range it now covers (or split it so each epic has its own breakdown file).
acceptance_criteria: Each listed file's top-of-doc status/title is consistent with its own last section or with a quick grep-based check (commit hashes for daf-unit; scheduler_providers.dart comments for overdue-refactor; test/e2e/journeys count for e2e-test-suite-plan).
No other action required — these are label-only fixes, not content rewrites.

finding.title: Update docs/qa/legacy auth scenarios and docs/planning upgrade-flow UX specs for the credential-less offline-account redesign

evidence.quote: Password hashed with argon2id, stored in local SQLite | None. No sync, no backup
AUTH-06: Email/password signup (local-born, airplane mode) ... Enter a password that meets strength requirements
The argon2id hash in SQLite is updated to the new password
For security, please enter your account password. This is the same password you use to sign in

finding.why: signup_screen.dart's offline path is documented in-code as credential-less ('no email, no password') per the 2026-06-14 product decision, confirmed still true today. All 6 docs above (linked from docs/index.md's active reference sections, none carrying a staleness banner) still describe/design around a password-based local-born account with argon2id verification. A tester running AUTH-06/SET-23 cannot find the password-entry UI they're told to test (false failure or wasted time); an engineer implementing the upgrade flow could copy ux-upgrade-flow-spec.md §5.2's 'verify existing password' step into new code, which cannot work once `passwordHash` is null for a credential-less account.
finding.recommendation: Add the same staleness-banner pattern already used well elsewhere in this repo (two-database-architecture.md, v1-developer-roadmap.md) to these 6 files, or rewrite the affected scenarios/screens to match the credential-less flow and the convert-on-reconnect upgrade entry point.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the 6 files carries a dated staleness banner pointing at the current onboarding/upgrade design, or its password-signup content is rewritten to match signup_screen.dart.
docs/index.md links only to auth docs that are current or explicitly marked historical.

finding.title: Reconcile qa/legacy and ux-patterns-quick-reference tutor-mode docs with the grant-based tutoring redesign

evidence.quote: all 5 routes, `TutorPinGuard` active, 7 screens ... deprioritized ... no new investment
TUTOR-10 | P0 | Cannot mark completions in tutor mode
TRACK-10 | P1 | Activate tutor track prompts PIN setup
Tutor mode is read-only (FR100) while parent mode has full write access.

finding.why: grep confirms TutorPinGuard no longer exists anywhere in lib/ — superseded by an invite/accept/revoke M:N grant model under lib/features/tutoring/ (tutor_grant.dart, tutor_pin_entry_gate.dart, invite_tutor_screen.dart, manage_tutors_screen.dart). The 'deprioritized, no new investment' claim in 11-tutor-mode.md's own callout is itself now contradicted by this same repo's later planning docs (tutor-mode-brief.md 2026-05-20, tutor-talmid-view-plan 2026-05-26, tutor-edit-propagation-plan 2026-05-28), whose trackers record a completed multi-week rebuild that also gave tutors Manage-Tracks and Bulk-prior write access beyond 'strictly read-only.' A tester using these docs looks for a self-service Settings PIN flow that no longer exists, and would flag the now-intentional edit capability as a regression against a stale spec.
finding.recommendation: Mark 11-tutor-mode.md and the tutor cross-references in 05-multi-track.md/10-parent-mode.md as superseded by the grant-based model (or move 11-tutor-mode.md fully under docs/_archive, matching the existing Epic-11 archive entry), and correct the ux-patterns-quick-reference.md route-guard table.
acceptance_criteria: 11-tutor-mode.md's banner reflects the grant-based redesign instead of asserting 'no new investment,' or the file moves to docs/_archive.

finding.title: Rewrite docs/planning/testing-quick-reference.md — it teaches the banned mockito pattern and cites nonexistent files
finding.why: coding-standards.md TQ-4 bans new mockito; the live suite has 0 mockito imports and 182 mocktail-based test files, so every worked example in this doc uses the disallowed framework. It is dated 2026-02-08 with no staleness marker and is linked from docs/index.md's 'Planning and design' section (described there as reflecting 'the current code'). None of the concrete files it cites (curriculum_card.dart, mishnayos_adapter.dart, the adapters/ directory) exist in lib/, and its 'API Tests (Sefaria)' section describes a runtime HTTP-fetch content architecture that contradicts the actual build-time-bundled content design confirmed in docs/qa/legacy/07-content-browsing.md (FR6). A contributor or AI agent following this doc would reintroduce a banned test framework and reference dead paths.
finding.recommendation: Rewrite against current mocktail-based test helpers and real file paths, or replace with a pointer to the current testing guide plus a superseded banner in the meantime.
acceptance_criteria: The doc contains zero `package:mockito` code examples.
Every **File:** path cited resolves to a real file under lib/ or test/.
